prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
Sorry to hear about your accident — that’s stressful. I can help you pick the right lawyer, but I need a bit more information first so my recommendations are useful.

Quick questions
- What injuries did you suffer and were you treated in a hospital? (Minor, moderate, serious/permanent)
- When did the crash happen?
- Where in Pleasanton did it occur and was a police report filed?
- Was the other driver insured? Do you have their info/witnesses/photos?
- Do you already have an insurer adjuster contacting you or have you given any recorded statements?
- Do you prefer a local Pleasanton/tri‑Valley lawyer, or is an East Bay / Oakland–San Jose firm okay?
- Any preferences: small firm vs. large, trial experience vs. settlements only, language needs, budget concerns?

How to choose the right lawyer (short checklist)
- Specialization: pick an attorney who focuses on auto/personal injury (not general practice).
- Experience and results: look for past settlements/verdicts in similar injury cases.
- Communication: choose someone who returns calls and explains strategy in plain language.
- Trial experience: many cases settle, but hire a lawyer who will try the case if needed.
- Fees: most personal injury lawyers work on contingency. Typical rates are 33%–40% plus costs; get the exact fee and who pays expenses if you lose.
- Client reviews and ethics: check State Bar records (discipline) and online reviews (Google, Yelp, Martindale).
- Local knowledge: familiarity with Pleasanton/Alameda/Contra Costa courts and local adjusters/judges can help.

What to bring to a consultation
- Police report number
- Photos of the crash/vehicle damage/injuries
- Medical records and bills or a list of providers and dates
- Insurance info (yours and the other party’s)
- Names/contact of witnesses
- Any communication from insurers or the at-fault party

Immediate steps you should take now (if not already done)
- Get any needed medical care and follow doctors’ orders (important for claims).
- Preserve evidence: photos, damaged parts, clothing, medical records.
- Don’t give recorded statements to the other side/insurer without your lawyer.
- Note deadlines: in California you generally have 2 years from the injury to sue (Code of Civil Procedure §335.1).

If you want, I can:
- Search for 3–5 vetted local Pleasanton / Tri‑Valley personal injury lawyers and give short pros/cons for each.
- Draft a short list of questions to ask during free consultations.
Tell me the answers to the quick questions above and whether you want a local shortlist, and I’ll prepare specific attorney recommendations.
